problem: 'short decision points' is unclear and mixes up the idea: it is the number and complexity of decision points that matter, not their length.
fix: Layout with clear paths, open sightlines and few decision points reduces wrong turns.

problem: 'Keep one aid per decision point' is ambiguous; a reader may think only one sign may exist in the whole world.
fix: Do not stack several aids at the same decision point; one clear aid per junction is enough.

problem: 'The user moves through the scene, while objects stay fixed' is contradicted later by world scaling, where the world appears to shrink or grow around a nearly stationary user.
fix: In most travel techniques the user moves through the scene while objects stay fixed; in world scaling the world itself is resized around the user.

where: Exam traps, user-centred versus environment-centred aids
problem: Signs are listed as user-centred aids here, but signs are physically placed in the world, so some syllabi call them environment-centred; the chapter does not warn of this split.
fix: Add: interface aids such as maps and guides are user-centred; signs, lighting and landmarks are placed in the world and some syllabi call them environment-centred.
